newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool indicator rises 7 cents to 667c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool indicator rises 7 cents to 667c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose seven cents to 667 cents a kg clean on Wednesday at sales in Sydney and Adelaide, Wool International said.
Merino fleece gained, with 19/24 microns up to one percent dearer, 20/21/22/23m 1.5 percent dearer, and 25/26m slightly dearer, with merino skirtings generally unchanged.
In crossbreds, 27/31m were slightly dearer, 28/29m unchanged and 30m slightly cheaper.
In cardings, lambs were unchanged, locks generally unchanged, and crutchings slightly cheaper.
WI said Japanese interests including China were principal buyers with strong support from local mills and Taiwan.
Of the 25,793 bales offered, 8.1 percent were passed in.
In early Fremantle selling, 20/23m merino fleece were two percent cheaper, 21/22m three percent cheaper and 24m 2.5 percent cheaper.
The early pass-in rate was 11 percent, WI said.
Sales continue on Thursday in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle with about 37,400 bales to be offered.
